This role focuses on spacecraft and launch vehicle structural dynamics, coupled loads analysis, finite element analysis (FEA), modal analysis, vibration and acoustic testing, mechanical shock, and flight hardware qualification using NASTRAN, FEMAP, MATLAB, Python, and related engineering tools. Responsibilities include evaluating structural loads, dynamic environments, analytical models, hardware test results, model correlation, and verification evidence to determine flight readiness. Candidates must bring extensive aerospace structural analysis experience and practical flight hardware testing expertise. The position may be filled at the Senior Engineer or Subject Matter Expert (SME) level based on experience and technical qualifications. Conduct and evaluate coupled loads analysis (CLA), finite element analysis (FEA), modal analysis, and structural dynamics assessments for aerospace flight hardware. Develop and review finite element models, evaluating mass properties, stiffness, damping, boundary conditions, load paths, interfaces, model fidelity, and sensitivities. Analyze modal, transient, frequency response, sine vibration, random vibration, acoustic, and mechanical shock environments associated with launch and spaceflight operations. Evaluate quasi-static loads, inertial acceleration (g-loads), structural responses, and dynamic amplification affecting spacecraft, payloads, components, and interfaces. Assess acoustic loading environments and test results, including sound pressure levels (SPL), frequency-dependent acoustic spectra, and structural responses. Evaluate random vibration power spectral density (PSD), acceleration responses, test tolerances, notching strategies, response limits, and qualification or acceptance criteria. Analyze mechanical shock environments using shock response spectra (SRS), time-history data, hardware response measurements, and applicable verification requirements. Identify critical structural modes, load paths, dynamic sensitivities, interface loads, acceleration levels, and potential structural failure mechanisms. Manipulate mass and stiffness matrices and develop reduced-order dynamic models using Component Mode Synthesis, Craig-Bampton reduction, and related analytical techniques. Support and independently assess flight hardware structural and environmental testing, including modal surveys, vibration, acoustic, shock, and other dynamic qualification tests. Review test requirements, plans, procedures, instrumentation, input environments, response limits, acceptance criteria, and technical reports to evaluate hardware qualification and flight readiness. Perform pre-test analytical predictions, post-test data evaluations, and structural model correlation using measured flight hardware or flight-like hardware responses. Investigate test anomalies, exceedances, unexpected structural responses, and verification discrepancies; assess root causes, hardware impacts, corrective actions, retest requirements, and flight rationale. Identify bounding test environments, critical modes, sensitive interfaces, off-nominal conditions, and potential failure modes to improve analytical and verification coverage. Develop and review structural test plans, qualification and acceptance criteria, engineering procedures, verification documentation, and technical reports. Experience using structural analysis and finite element modeling software such as NASTRAN, FEMAP, or comparable engineering tools. Experience using Python, MATLAB, C, C++, or similar engineering analysis and scripting tools. Experience supporting structural or environmental testing of flight hardware or flight-like aerospace hardware, including test planning, execution, data evaluation, or analytical model correlation. Knowledge of acoustic loading, random vibration, mechanical shock, quasi-static loads, inertial acceleration environments, and aerospace structural response. Experience interpreting random vibration PSDs, shock response spectra, acoustic sound pressure levels, acceleration responses, dynamic amplification, and structural modes. Ability to independently evaluate complex analytical models, including assumptions, inputs, boundary conditions, methodologies, fidelity, sensitivities, and engineering conclusions. Ability to translate structural dynamics analyses and test results into engineering assessments of hardware risks, structural margins, qualification status, and flight readiness. Demonstrated technical judgment in evaluating complex aerospace engineering issues and independently assessing structural analysis and test evidence. Ability to communicate technically defensible engineering findings, risks, and recommendations to multidisciplinary engineering teams, customers, and program leadership. Ability to collaborate across engineering disciplines while maintaining the independent technical judgment required for objective engineering assessments. Preferred Qualifications: Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering , Aerospace Engineering, or a related engineering discipline. Experience analyzing spacecraft, launch vehicles, lunar landers, payloads, or other flight hardware exposed to launch and spaceflight dynamic environments. Experience with modal surveys, sine vibration, random vibration, acoustic testing, mechanical shock testing, and structural model correlation. Experience supporting spacecraft or launch vehicle development through design reviews, verification, qualification, acceptance testing, anomaly resolution, and flight readiness. Proficiency with MSC Nastran, Simcenter Nastran, FEMAP, or equivalent finite element and structural dynamics software. Experience with Component Mode Synthesis, Craig-Bampton reduction, superelements, and reduced-order structural modeling. Experience developing, customizing, or automating structural engineering analysis processes through scripting or software development. Experience independently evaluating engineering analyses, qualification testing, and verification evidence produced by spacecraft manufacturers, launch vehicle providers, or other aerospace organizations. review_candidates.title: Responsable Infrastructure & SSI
review_candidates.description: Qui sommes-nous ? Implantée depuis plus de 120 ans en Lorraine, St Hubert est une PME française engagée, aujourd’hui leader sur le marché de la margarine. Notre mission ? Partager le goût de bien manger en proposant des produits qui allient plaisir, qualité et équilibre, portés par la passion et l’engagement de nos 200 collaborateurs. Rejoindre St Hubert, c’est intégrer une entreprise qui place l’humain, la simplicité et la responsabilité au cœur de ses actions. C’est faire partie d’une équipe soudée, animée par un savoir-faire historique et une envie commune de bâtir une crémerie d’avenir , innovante et responsable. Votre Rôle Placé(e) sous la responsabilité du Directeur des Systèmes d’Information (DSI), vous garantissez la disponibilité, la performance et la sécurité des infrastructures informatiques de l’entreprise. Vous pilotez l’exploitation des environnements techniques, définissez et mettez en œuvre la politique de sécurité des systèmes d’information (SSI) en étroite collaboration avec le DSI et accompagnez les évolutions technologiques de l’organisation. Vous encadrez également l’activité de support informatique et veillez à la qualité des services délivrés aux utilisateurs. Vos Missions Infrastructure & Exploitation Garantir le maintien en conditions opérationnelles, la disponibilité et la performance des infrastructures IT (serveurs, réseaux, télécommunications, postes de travail et équipements mobiles), dans le respect des engagements de qualité de service (SLA). Piloter l’administration, l’exploitation et la supervision des infrastructures techniques, ainsi que la gestion des incidents et des dispositifs de sauvegarde et de restauration. Assurer la gestion et l’optimisation du parc informatique et téléphonique, en maîtrisant les coûts, les ressources et les performances. Définir, en collaboration avec le DSI, les orientations d’architecture technique et piloter les projets d’évolution des infrastructures, en coordination avec les prestataires externes. Sécurité des Systèmes d’Information (RSSI) Définir conjointement avec le DSI la politique de sécurité des systèmes d’information, en assurer la mise en œuvre et l’évolution, dans le respect des exigences réglementaires, des normes et des bonnes pratiques applicables. Piloter la prévention et la gestion des risques cyber, notamment à travers les audits de sécurité, les analyses de vulnérabilité et le déploiement de solutions de protection adaptées. Définir et coordonner les dispositifs de continuité et de reprise d’activité (PCA/PRA), en veillant à la résilience du système d’information. Superviser la gestion des incidents de cybersécurité, coordonner les actions de remédiation et contribuer au pilotage des cellules de crise, en lien avec le DSI, en cas de menace avérée. Sensibiliser et accompagner la Direction et les collaborateurs aux enjeux de cybersécurité et aux bonnes pratiques de protection du système d’information. Management & Évolution technologique Encadrer, animer et accompagner l’équipe support informatique (2 personnes), en organisant ses activités, en développant ses compétences et en garantissant la qualité du service rendu aux utilisateurs. Assurer une veille sur les évolutions technologiques (infrastructures, réseaux, télécommunications, cybersécurité, intelligence artificielle, digitalisation et dématérialisation) et identifier les opportunités d’amélioration pour l’entreprise. Être force de proposition et accompagner les projets d’innovation et de transformation technologique, en cohérence avec les orientations définies par le DSI et les besoins des métiers. Profil recherché : Formation supérieure en (Bac+4/5). Expérience significative sur un poste similaire dans un contexte industriel mêlant infrastructure, exploitation et cybersécurité. Solides compétences en systèmes, réseaux, sécurité et pilotage de prestataires. Expérience du management d’équipe technique. Leadership, sens du service, rigueur et capacité à gérer les situations de crise. CDI à pourvoir dès maintenant au sein d’une entreprise reconnue et à taille humaine . Des locaux modernes à Paris 14ème : rooftop, salle de sport, salle de sieste, espace jeux vidéo et restaurant d’entreprise. 2 jours de télétravail par semaine pour favoriser l’équilibre entre vie professionnelle et vie personnelle. Une vie d’entreprise riche et conviviale, rythmée par un calendrier d’événements tout au long de l’année (team buildings, afterworks, événements sportifs, etc.). Une culture conviviale et engagée, portée par des actions RSE, l’innovation et le plaisir de travailler ensemble. Des missions à impact, au sein d’équipes bienveillantes où la collaboration et l’initiative sont valorisées. Déroulement des entretiens Un premier échange de préqualification RH de 30 minutes en visioconférence (Teams), afin de faire connaissance, d’échanger sur votre parcours et vos motivations, et de vous présenter plus en détail le poste ainsi que l’entreprise St Hubert. Un entretien d’1h30 en présentiel avec le manager et/ou un membre de l’équipe, pour approfondir votre expérience, échanger sur les missions du poste et vous permettre de découvrir l’équipe et son fonctionnement. Un entretien de 30 minutes avec le N+2 et/ou membre de l’équipe industrielle, afin de compléter les échanges, partager la vision plus globale de l’organisation et valider l’adéquation entre votre profil et les enjeux du poste. Qui sont-ils ? St Hubert, c’est une aventure qui a débuté en 1904 à Nancy ! Aujourd’hui, nous continuons d’innover pour vous offrir des produits qui allient plaisir et nutrition. Près de 120 ans plus tard, c’est toujours en Lorraine, à Ludres, qu’est concentré l’essentiel de nos activités de production sur un site moderne, efficace et flexible. Chez nous, chaque instant mérite d’être savouré, et chaque repas doit être un plaisir à partager. Nos produits contribuent à des moments de convivialité, de plaisir, et de bien-être avec ceux que l’on aime ! Notre engagement envers nos consommateurs, la planète, est ancré dans nos valeurs et fait écho à notre vision de construire une crémerie d’avenir. Avec des matières premières de qualité et une approche novatrice, nous avançons vers un futur toujours plus responsable, en accord avec les enjeux de notre époque, en végétalisant l’assiette des Français. Nos références phares, comme St Hubert Oméga 3®, St Hubert 41, et la toute nouvelle gamme St Hubert Épaisse, se distinguent par leur capacité à allier plaisir et praticité, en répondant aux besoins de ceux qui recherchent une alternative savoureuse et gourmande, sans compromis sur la qualité. St Hubert est également présent en Italie via la marque Valle’®, Leader du marché des matières grasses végétales à tartiner et des pâtes à dérouler. Notre siège est basé à Paris, et notre force de vente est pleinement dédiée au territoire français, portée par une équipe engagée et proche du terrain.

General Summary Of Position The LAC Regional Programs Manager (RPM) is responsible for the overall management, program direction, reporting, and stewardship of AFSC resources in the countries we work in throughout Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC). This role contributes to program coordination, management, supervision, representation, networking, and reporting, ensuring alignment with AFSC's mission, values, and strategic priorities. They are responsible for managing relationships with program partners as well as assessing partners’ ability and as necessary improving their capacity along the program management cycle. The Regional Programs Manager participates in dialogues with government ministries, United Nations agencies, European Union authorities, relevant country embassies, and local and international NGOs, according to priorities set by the Regional Director and in coordination with the Policy Education and Advocacy Coordinator (PEAC). Within the AFSC norm of collaborative decision making and mutual support, the representative will function as part of a team, together with the Regional Director and with staff working based in Philadelphia and other IP regions to ensure that there are strong partnerships with increased capacity for effective delivery of our programs at regional level. Essential Functions / Responsibilities And Accountabilities Strategic Program Leadership, Planning and Management: Plan, develop, and provide overall management and coordination for AFSC's programs in the LAC region, within the context of AFSC's regional and global strategic directions, Theories of Change, and Action. Provide strategic vision of AFSC's Programs and works, standardize program practices across, and operation models across the LAC region to ensure consistent, high-quality program implementation, meeting standards in the region for program management, HR, finance, security, health and safety. Define, develop and implement regional program policies, guidelines and procedures. Ensure proper planning, monitoring and evaluation of the programs, including the use of lessons learned to improve programming in close coordination with the Regional Officer for Program Support, Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning. Encourages constant context analysis to identify program opportunities and priorities. Ensure timely submission of all required program narrative and financial reports. Participates in advocacy strategies to influence changes at local, national and international level in coordination with the PEAC. Ensures that program plans and budgets are in place, that costs are kept within budgets, and that their supervises provide regular, consistently high-quality reports to RD. Provides leadership and guidance to the program officers in the implementation of programs and documentation in line with AFSC´s values, policies, and procedures. Ensure that program and project proposals are consistent in accordance with the program budgets and cost effective. Identifies opportunities for AFSC LAC to engage with international, regional and national networks to enhance and strengthen LAC programs. Acts as a liaison between the programmatic team in the region and programmatic teams in other AFSC’s regions and offices, to promote, facilitate and support collaborative and strategic actions among regions. Communicates regularly with the Regional Director to discuss program, financial and administrative issues. Represents AFSC in meetings, events or forums related to LAC program’s topics or per request of the Regional Director. Partnership And Capacity Building Responsible for managing relationships with program partners, assessing their ability, and improving their capacity through the program management cycle. Develop new partnerships and collaborative approaches to enhance program work and strengthen the ability of committed partner organizations to work together to achieve common goals. Regional Team Leadership & Development Ensure AFSC staff members effectively apply Quaker Values and conflict-sensitive, non-violence approaches and methodologies to their work. Lead a regional program organization where team members can effectively manage programs across multiple territories, not limited to their specific geographic location. Foster a regional organizational culture that includes career development plans, clear roles and responsibilities, and opportunities for high-impact contributions, motivating staff and creating a long-term commitment to AFSC. Manages program officers and Regional Officer for Program Support, Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning efficiently and within AFSC’s legal parameters, delegating authority where appropriate and ensuring that staff members are given opportunities for development and training, as discussed and agreed. Develops and maintains a healthy environment for the team, coordinating timely discussions on strategic programming issues and guaranteeing that the staff members reflect the institutional character in their relationships with partner organizations and allies. Ensures excellent people management and development of staff managed, in accordance with performance management cycle and policies on development of staff, and capacity building plans. Coordinates with the Operations Regional Manager on country administrative, financial and program staff and oversees the management of personnel matters through appropriate internal structures and procedures. Performance Management & Results Orientation Define and implement Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), dashboards, and other tools to effectively manage program operations and outcomes, proactively driving continuous improvement. Financial Management, Fundraising & Reporting Implement Fund Raising strategies in close collaboration with the Regional Director and development team. Prepares information that supports program proposals for fundraising and reports on the use of funds to the donor agencies in coordination with the Regional Officer for Program Support, Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning. Manages budget control and ensures that sound financial and accounting procedures are followed. Gives input for the preparation of required financial reports, and information for audits; provides timely information on changes that affect program implementation and expenditure. Align with the Communications team or consultants to document and present program impact, supporting advocacy and fundraising efforts. Cooperate with Finance on financial control, providing required information for accounting, reporting, and compliance. Works with the Regional Operations Manager to develop budgets for funding proposals, ensuring consistency with program objectives and donor requirements. Risk Management Ensures an appropriate risk-threat assessment of the delivery program considering staff security, partners security, reputational and communication risks and others. Monitors and analyses the context and designs, in coordination with the RD, program officers, the strategies for managing the identified risks in line with AFSC Security Policy. Monitors of the implementation of the security protocols in place, leads to systematic reviews and recommends changes. Participates in the Security Task Force group for LAC in coordination with RD. Facilitate capacity building in safety and security for staff in coordination with the Safety and Security Director. Emergency Response Inform the Regional Director about emergencies occurring in the region, with special attention to the defined program intervention areas. Designs the first assessment of the situation to report to the RD to present to the Emergency Response Team. Contribute to the drawn-up process of the “Initial Response Plan” that the RD will present to the AGS-IP aligned to the AFSC's Emergency Response guidelines, in close coordination with the LAC Emergency Response Team. AFSC Alignment Work in consultation with the staff of the Human Resources and Inclusion Department, and other staff as appropriate, to determine and apply regionally, and country specific relevant affirmative action policies to regional staffing, administrative functioning and program within the region. Understanding of and commitment to the principles, concerns, and considerations of AFSC regarding issues of race, class, nationality, religion, age, gender and sexual orientation, and disabilities. Demonstrated ability to work and communicate with diverse staff. Candidates must demonstrate a strong commitment to AFSC's core values of peace, justice, equality, and non-violence and understanding of the belief in the intrinsic worth of every individual. Minimum Experience And Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Nonprofit Management, Social Studies, Peace Building, International Relations/affairs, Law, or closely related field. Ability to work independently in an unstructured setting and program, yet within a framework of long-distance communication, consultation, and decision making. Experience in leading and motivating geographically remote teams; and program strategy through partners in challenging locations. Ability to cope in situations of high risk and in compliance with security measures, to work under pressure, and to organize time effectively. Experience effectively managing grants through the whole cycle of Grants management (desirable).
